Each generated case is listed separately.

Inventory destinations that do not exist: apps/avelune_studio/lib/platform/rendering/viewports/presentation_canvas_surface.dart (for presentation_canvas.dart) and .../viewports/cinematic_path_painter_surface.dart (for cinematic_path_painter.dart). The 'render_separate' extraction target is therefore not there; both files are verdicted pure_ui/logic_already_owned on their own merit.

Inventory disagrees with reading: cinematic_inspector_camera.dart is classed ui_retire with no destination but holds the 'actor:'/'point:'/'center' codec and focus defaults; cinematic_transport_listenable.dart and presentation_transport_listenable.dart are plain Listenable adapters (pure_ui, not mixed). cinematic_view_state.dart and presentation_view_state.dart name world_draft_inputs.dart as destination, which is unrelated (only a bare invalidFields set).

Legacy refusal vs owner clamp: PresentationTimeline refuses an out-of-bounds drag ('Déplacement refusé', no command) whereas PresentationTimelineEditingController clamps/snap-bounds the preview and emits a command. No non-legacy test pins either; a product decision is needed before deleting ui11_presentation_transport_controls_test 'a refused timeline drag...'.

2D vs 3D point drag semantics differ: cinematic_point_handle.dart rounds the destination to whole cells (round(point + delta/cell)); cinematic_spatial_map_scene.dart uses point + integer cell delta (keeps the fractional part of the point) and reports taps at cell centre (+.5). The tests (cinematic_spatial_gestures_ui10_test for 2D vs cinematic_spatial_map_scene_test for 3D) each pin one of them; neither is pinned outside legacy.

Initial camera for the playback viewport is built in the legacy widgets with a window clamped to the map (min(15,w) x min(11,h) in cinematic_playback_viewport.dart; fixed 15x11 in cinematic_spatial_map_scene.dart). cinematics_ui10_preview_runtime_parity_test (non-legacy) builds its projection with a fixed 15*cell x 11*cell window on a large map, so it cannot detect the clamp. This is the one place where Studio and Player could diverge on small maps.

cinematic_inspector.dart#_edit re-injects stageContext.manualPaths after every inspector edit. map_core already preserves them in updateCinematicTimelineActorMoveStep (cinematic_actor_move_facing_test: 'editing facing duration or motion preserves a manual route and preview'), and the controller has the same _keepPaths privately for its own methods. The wrapper looks redundant for move/jump/facing edits but is the only protection for other inspector edits (unsure); extract/replace deliberately.

The inspector re-implements range validation already enforced by the owner (jump height <=4, jump duration 200..30000: map_core cinematicTimelineActorJump*/cinematicTimelineMaximumDurationMs) with different messages ('La durée du saut doit être comprise entre 200 et 30000 ms.' vs the owner's ArgumentError). The legacy tests assert on the UI messages (contains 'hauteur', 'durée du saut', 'strictement positive'); the owner texts differ for the last one.

ui11_presentation_field_guard_test, canvas_gesture_test, responsive_test and busy_test import tapUi11 from ui11_presentation_widget_test.dart (cross-test import): the helper must move or die with the widget test when these are retired.

support/ui11_widget_port.dart and support/ui10_widget_port.dart are in blast.json only through support/m2_ui_fixture.dart, which imports lib/presentation/features/map_workspace/map_workspace_screen.dart and presentation/theme/studio_theme.dart (other zone). Their own code is legacy-free and reusable.

Non-blast owner tests used as coverage also exist in packages/map_editor (presentation_timeline_editing_controller_test, presentation_studio_timeline_test). I only cite the controller-level (widget-free) one; map_editor's presentation_studio_timeline_test pilots a different UI (map_editor widgets), not Avelune Studio's.

Not a legacy-UI dependency but visible: ui11_presentation_library_test.dart (non-blast) proves layer ordering/archive/restore through PresentationWorkspaceController, and ui11_fixture_test.dart proves the fixture; both stay valid after the retirement.

I did not find any non-legacy test for allowMobileActorCrossing through the Studio controller (covered in map_core/map_authoring/map_runtime only), nor for CinematicLibrary filtering, nor for presentation consumers() list.
